name: MathlibAnnex.CStarAlgebra.CAR.separableCounterexampleRepresentation_injective
title: Faithfulness of the representation on the CAR trace Hilbert space

content.display_title: Faithfulness of the representation on the CAR trace Hilbert space
content.one_sentence_role: Proves that the representation $\widetilde\rho:T\to B(H_\tau)$ is injective.
content.natural_language_statement: Let $A$ be the completed CAR algebra and $T=C^*(\pi(A)\cup\{L_i:i\in I\})\subseteq B(\mathcal H)$ the algebra generated by the selected direct sum $\pi$ of pure-state GNS representations indexed by their unitary-equivalence classes $i\in I$ and the unitaries $L_i$ from the fixed homogeneity and shell construction. Write $\iota(a)=\pi(a)$ for the embedding $A\to T$. Let $\tau$ be the CAR trace and $\phi$ its chosen state extension to $T$. Write $\rho_\phi:T\to B(H_\phi)$ for the GNS representation of $\phi$, and use the chosen unitary $E:H_\tau=L^2(A,\tau)\to H_\phi$ from the cited trace construction. For $\widetilde\rho(t)=E^{-1}\rho_\phi(t)E$, $$\widetilde\rho(s)=\widetilde\rho(t)\ \Longrightarrow\ s=t\qquad(s,t\in T).$$
content.assumptions: The automorphisms and unitaries defining $T$ are those fixed by CAR homogeneity. The cited injectivity theorem for the conjugated GNS representation applies to every such shell family, hence to this one.
content.conclusion: Thus $\widetilde\rho:T\to B(H_\tau)$ is faithful. Together with the separately established separability of $H_\tau$, it realizes this same $T$ faithfully on a separable Hilbert space.
content.proof_summary: Cancel the fixed unitary conjugation and use faithfulness of the GNS representation $\rho_\phi$ of the state extension.

proof_steps.text: If $\widetilde\rho(s)=\widetilde\rho(t)$, then $$\rho_\phi(s)=E\widetilde\rho(s)E^{-1}=E\widetilde\rho(t)E^{-1}=\rho_\phi(t).$$ The cited injectivity theorem for $\rho_\phi$ gives $s=t$. The Lean proof specializes this same argument to the fixed family.

content.lean_realization_notes: This statement concerns injectivity of a representation, not faithfulness of a vector state, and does not assert irreducibility.
